issues.problem: hanu is 'jaw', not 'chin' (ठोड़ी); gloss and English say 'jaws'.
'in flesh' is an explanatory addition not in gūḍha-jatruḥ (gloss: 'with hidden collar-bones'); Hindi is literal.
Concessive 'भी' (even though) is added; the Sanskrit has only the participle niyujyamānaḥ, and the English does not add 'although'.

Stated as fact, but asya can equally be the genitive of the recipient (Bharata: 'gave the sandals to him as a trust for the kingdom'), which is how commentators commonly take it; the Hindi 'अपनी' silently chooses the first reading.
issues.fix: append a note that both readings of asya are possible

patch.text: asya may also be the genitive of the recipient (Bharata): 'having given the sandals to him as a trust for the kingdom'; the line does not decide.

issues.problem: The flag pairs the single token 'agastya' with the replacement 'agastyabhrātaraṃ'; applied per token this would duplicate bhrātaraṃ. The flagged src should be the two-token span 'agastya bhrātaraṃ' (join, no space).
Vocative rāvaṇa is rendered 'हे रावण' in Hindi but bare 'Rāvaṇa' in English; the fixed-rendering convention (rājan = 'O king') calls for 'O Rāvaṇa'.
issues.fix: "O Rāvaṇa, enmity with him, that mighty one, is not advisable for you."

summary: 40 units checked (tokens, splits, gloss/gram, Hindi, English, flags, notes, confidence). Splits and sandhi are correct throughout; grammar labels are sound (abhyāgaman as aorist, anavāpya with -ya after negation, tūṇī as i-stem dual, loc./gen. absolutes all right). Both text_flags (14: -jño before s-; 32: ekāgre vs ekāgro) are reasonable and marked medium. Issues: 1 error (unit 8 Hindi adds 'एक पुरुष है, जो'), 8 minor (4 Hindi/English sense mismatch for anasūyaka; 6 Hindi drops ca; 9 ठोड़ी for hanu; 10 'in flesh' added; 29 added भी; 30 note asserts asya = Rāma's where the recipient reading is at least as likely; 33 text_flag span mis-stated; 40 missing vocative 'O'). No invented Sanskrit, no imported story, names and numbers exact (fourteen thousand). No regrouping suggested: 18-19, 26-27 and 37-38 are sentence pairs but the edition's per-verse grouping is kept and the notes cross-reference correctly.
